payload.summary: Cycle 2 makes a strong conceptual improvement by collapsing the work into one capability and one gated Issue, defining a finite inventory cutoff, choosing the repository's actual Burrito/GitHub artifact channel, and requiring fail-closed immutable publication. It still cannot pass because that complete hierarchy is not executable or authorized as stored: proposal version 2 is only proposed while approval and Issue authorization remain bound to version 1; structured execution fields are empty; Issue 60 retains its stale, incomplete body; the proposed window conflicts with the inherited window; and a mandatory `make all` gate has no Makefile. The release sequence also needs one unambiguous owner/order across tag-triggered workflow publication and BOS deployment/verification/release operations. These are concrete contract and verifiability defects, not requests for additional work items.

findings.title: Version 2 is proposed but only version 1 is approved and inherited
findings.evidence: bos_get_goal_execution reports proposal version 2 with status proposed, while the sole approval is explicitly bound to proposalVersion 1. Issue 60's active inheritedAuthorization is also bound to version 1 and ends at 2026-08-16T22:00:00Z, whereas version 2 proposes execution through 2026-08-18T20:45:00Z. The execution proposal's structured capabilities, issues, dependencies, repositories, requiredValidations, requiredReviewers, riskTags, irreversibleActions, productOutcome, expected/max duration, and expected/max token fields remain empty/null; their intended values exist only as free-form scope strings.
findings.request: Persist a structurally complete versioned execution contract (or establish that the consumer deterministically parses and enforces the encoded scope schema), bind the reviewed version to the authenticated decision, and re-inherit the exact same version/window/budget into Issue 60 before execution. Do not treat the version-1 approval as approval of version 2.

findings.title: The single-Issue hierarchy is not materialized in the executable Issue
findings.evidence: The planning proposal sensibly simplifies delivery to one capability and one Issue with five ordered gates, but bos_get_issue(60) still says integration is already complete and scopes only candidate verification, PR/merge, and release/production verification. Its four acceptance criteria omit the frozen inventory ledger, disposition rules, integration/provenance map, version 0.2.2, release hardening, exact commands, conditional reviews, artifact matrix, and gate handoffs. It has no dependencies and is currently agent:blocked with an active version-1 claim.
findings.request: Update the executable Issue/contract so the sole work item itself contains the full ordered gate hierarchy and durable handoff artifacts, removing the contradicted assumption that integration is complete. Keeping one Issue is the simpler valid design; do not create a parallel shadow hierarchy.

findings.title: A mandatory QA command does not exist and several gates lack deterministic implementations
findings.evidence: The proposal requires `repository make all/full gates`, but repository inspection finds no Makefile or makefile. `.bos/project.yaml` defines only the mandatory `cd elixir && mise exec -- mix test` command. `mix.exs` exposes the `specs.check` alias path, while the proposal's owned-child leak scan, security-boundary assertions, release-workflow tests, inventory audit, and clean-install smoke receipt do not identify exact commands, scripts, baseline ownership rules, environments, or artifact schemas.
findings.request: Replace `make all` with commands that exist at the candidate cutoff, or explicitly add and validate that gate as candidate work. Provide an applicability/command/artifact matrix for every required validation, including exact process ownership/baseline rules and objective pass/fail thresholds; avoid duplicating mix test/coverage/spec work without a stated reason.

findings.title: The inventory universe is finite in principle but still not reproducibly enumerable
findings.evidence: The checkout is at origin/main d5c51b4b225c0b4b4335556eccbc0a1ab3850549 with many divergent origin refs. The two previously named consolidation/release refs are behind main by 3 and 22 commits respectively and have zero commits ahead. The proposal says to capture all local Symphony worktree roots and refs at a cutoff, but does not name the authoritative filesystem roots/common git directories, remote fetch/prune procedure, ledger storage/schema, or treatment of refs that are provider-visible but absent from the local clone. `git worktree list` in this checkout currently exposes only this worktree, which is not affirmative evidence that every user worktree universe is covered.
findings.request: Name the authoritative repository/common-git-dir and filesystem search roots, fetch policy and remote namespace, immutable cutoff procedure, ledger location/schema, and completeness proof. Record dirty, untracked, unreadable, missing, and provider-only states without cleanup. Candidate identity must remain an inventory output, not one of the stale named refs.

findings.title: Release immutability is planned but the governed provider sequence is internally inconsistent
findings.evidence: The current `.github/workflows/burrito-release.yml` uses `gh release upload "$TAG" ... --clobber` when a release exists, so hardening is genuinely required. However the workflow itself automatically creates the GitHub Release on tag push, while the execution prose separately says BOS/game-api should reserve/create the tag/release once and later calls `bos_create_release` after DeploymentVerification. Repository policy says deployment/release is incomplete until exact-commit DeploymentVerification passes, but the proposal treats artifact publication as the canonical production outcome and places post-publication verification before terminalization without identifying the exact BOS deployment/verification operations compatible with a tag-triggered workflow.
findings.request: Define one idempotent owner and exact dependency order for tag creation, workflow-triggered build/publication, BOS Deployment, DeploymentVerification, and BOS Release receipt. Specify collision behavior for tag, release, individual assets, and partial workflow reruns. Ensure game-api remains the exclusive provider interface for orchestration and that no step requires direct runner `gh` use outside the governed workflow.

findings.title: Broad semantic-area and reviewer lists are not derived from the eventual diff
findings.evidence: The proposal pre-enumerates orchestrator, adapter, outbox, authorization, workspace, cancellation, telemetry, dashboard, tracker, and release paths, plus multiple reviewer roles, before the inventory establishes which histories are substantive. This risks expanding integration and review beyond the Goal while UI/browser applicability depends on both a configured target and a final UI diff. No configured runtime/browser target exists in `.bos/project.yaml`, which only names main and approval/verification policy.
findings.request: Make affected modules, targeted tests, and concurrency/recovery review mechanically derived from the frozen disposition ledger and final diff. Keep functional/quality, architecture/security, and release-integrity coverage, but allow one reviewer artifact to cover multiple roles when independence and required expertise are preserved. Record browser/server checks deterministically not applicable unless a concrete configured target is discovered before the irreversible boundary.
